entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Neferirkare Kakai was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh, the third king of the Fifth Dynasty. Neferirkare, the eldest son of Sahure with his consort Meretnebty, was known as Ranefer A before he came to the throne. He acceded the day after his father's death and reigned for eight to eleven years, sometime in the early to mid-25th century BCE. He was himself very likely succeeded by his eldest son, born of his queen Khentkaus II, the prince Ranefer B who would take the throne as king Neferefre. Neferirkare fathered another pharaoh, Nyuserre Ini, who took the throne after Neferefre's short reign and the brief rule of the poorly known Shepseskare.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Neferirkare Kakai's reign marked a transitional period in ancient Egyptian history, as he was succeeded by his son Neferefre and grandson Nyuserre Ini, who continued the dynasty's legacy. His eight to eleven year rule had a lasting impact on the development of the Fifth Dynasty.
